## File: README.md

# @mgpl-diagnostics/worker-kit

Background jobs for the MGPL Diagnostics backend. You define a job once (name, processor, retries,
how long its result is kept) and start it from one queue API. Underneath, the jobs run:

- on **BullMQ over Redis**, with `startWorker` in a separate worker process (production);
- **in-process**, with no Redis (development, tests, a single server);
- or **on the worker when it is available, otherwise standalone** (`fallbackBackend`), the
  behaviour mail-kit relies on.

All three behave the same: the same JSON data, the same retries and backoff, the same states and the
same error messages. `npm test` runs one scenario on each and compares the results.

- The main entry has **no runtime dependencies**. `bullmq` and `ioredis` are optional peers, used only
  by the `/bullmq` entry.
- Job data is checked in the caller: it must be JSON, under a size limit, and free of secret-looking
  keys (`password`, `token`, `secret`, …). Payloads carry ids; the processor looks things up.
- Processor failures are safe to show: a `JobFailure` keeps its message, anything else is logged and
  shown as "Job failed".

## Install

```bash
# .npmrc: @mgpl-diagnostics:registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com
npm install @mgpl-diagnostics/worker-kit
npm install bullmq ioredis   # only for the /bullmq entry
```

## Define jobs

```ts
import { defineJob, JobFailure } from "@mgpl-diagnostics/worker-kit";

export const renderInvoice = defineJob<{ orgId: string; invoiceId: string }, { base64: string }>({
  name: "invoice",
  queue: "documents",        // default: the name
  attempts: 2,               // default 3, exponential backoff from backoffMs (default 2 s)
  keepResultsMs: 3600_000,   // finished jobs readable for an hour (default); 0 = removed at once
  validate: (d) => { if (!d.invoiceId) throw new Error("invoiceId is required"); },
  async process(d, ctx) {    // ctx: { id, name, queue, attempt, attempts }
    const invoice = await services.billing.find(d.orgId, d.invoiceId);
    if (!invoice) throw new JobFailure("Invoice not found", false); // shown to the client, no retry
    return { base64: await render(invoice) };                        // must be JSON
  },
});
```

Data and results cross JSON on every backend, so a `Date` arrives as an ISO string.

## Start and read jobs

```ts
import { createJobQueue, fallbackBackend, inlineBackend } from "@mgpl-diagnostics/worker-kit";
import { bullmqBackend } from "@mgpl-diagnostics/worker-kit/bullmq";

const backend = process.env.REDIS_URL
  ? bullmqBackend({ redisUrl: process.env.REDIS_URL, prefix: "mgpl" })
  : inlineBackend();               // { wait: false } runs jobs in the background of this process

const jobs = createJobQueue({ backend, jobs: [renderInvoice, passwordReset] });

const job = await jobs.enqueue(renderInvoice, { orgId, invoiceId });
// → { id, name, queue, state, attempts, error, result, data, createdAt, finishedAt }
const later = await jobs.get(renderInvoice, job.id); // null if unknown, expired, or another job's id
```

Job ids are random UUIDs, but they are not a permission: check that the reader owns the job
(compare `data` with the session) before showing it.

With `inlineBackend()` (the default `wait: true`), `enqueue` resolves when the job has finished, so
the request waits. With BullMQ it resolves at once with `state: "waiting"`.

## Run the worker

```ts
import { startWorker } from "@mgpl-diagnostics/worker-kit/bullmq";

const worker = startWorker({
  redisUrl: process.env.REDIS_URL!,
  prefix: "mgpl",
  jobs: [renderInvoice, passwordReset], // one BullMQ Worker per queue
  concurrency: 4,
  onError: (e, ctx) => log.error({ err: e, job: ctx }, "job failed"), // errors that are not a JobFailure
});

process.once("SIGTERM", () => worker.close()); // finishes the jobs in hand, then stops
```

A `JobFailure` with `retry: false` fails the job at once (BullMQ `UnrecoverableError`); every other
failure uses the remaining attempts.

## Worker when available, standalone otherwise

```ts
import { redisConnection } from "@mgpl-diagnostics/worker-kit/bullmq";

const connection = redisConnection(process.env.REDIS_URL!);
const jobs = createJobQueue({
  backend: fallbackBackend({
    primary: bullmqBackend({ connection, prefix: "mgpl" }), // available() = connection is "ready"
    fallback: inlineBackend(),
    onFallback: (reason, job) => log.warn({ reason, job: job.def.name }, "ran without the worker"),
    // whenFails: "throw" → WorkerError WORKER_UNAVAILABLE instead
  }),
  jobs: [mailJob],
});
```

### With mail-kit

`jobs.enqueuer(job)` has mail-kit's `MailQueue` shape, so mail-kit can queue through worker-kit:

```ts
const mailJob = defineJob<MailJob, SendResult>({ name: "mail", keepResultsMs: 0, attempts: 5, backoffMs: 10_000,
  process: (job) => mailer.deliver(job) });
const mailer = createMailer({ transport, from, queue: jobs.enqueuer(mailJob) });
```

`keepResultsMs: 0` removes a mail job as soon as it is sent, because it can hold a reset link.
In mail-kit's MailJob the link sits under `data.link`, which is allowed; a key named `token` would be refused.

## Errors

`WorkerError.code` is a public contract (add, never rename):

| Code | When |
| --- | --- |
| `WORKER_UNKNOWN_JOB` | the job is not in this queue's `jobs` (or is a different definition with the same name) |
| `WORKER_BAD_DATA` | data is not JSON, too large, has a secret-looking key, or `validate` threw; bad job/queue name |
| `WORKER_DUPLICATE_JOB` | two definitions share a name |
| `WORKER_UNAVAILABLE` | `fallbackBackend` with `whenFails: "throw"`; an in-process `enqueuer` job failed; no Redis given |
| `WORKER_CLOSED` | the queue was closed |

## Develop

```bash
npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run build
npm run llms   # regenerate llms-full.txt (CI fails when it is stale)
```

`npm test` uses `REDIS_URL`, or starts a local `redis-server` when one is installed; without either the
BullMQ checks are skipped (CI sets `REQUIRE_REDIS=1` and a Redis service, so they always run there).

## File: AGENTS.md

# AGENTS.md — @mgpl-diagnostics/worker-kit

Background jobs for the MGPL Diagnostics backend: typed job definitions, one queue API over three
backends (BullMQ on Redis, in-process, worker-or-standalone fallback) and the worker runner.
**A library: no server, no GraphQL, no business logic.** The api repo defines the jobs and wires
them (container + `src/worker.ts`); mail-kit queues through `enqueuer()`.

## Map

```
src/types.ts      JobDefinition, JobInfo, JobState, JobContext, JobBackend, PreparedJob
src/errors.ts     WorkerError (codes), JobFailure (safe message + retry flag), isJobFailure
src/define.ts     defineJob, SECRET_KEY, toJsonData / prepareJob (checks in the caller), runAttempt, backoffDelay
src/queue.ts      createJobQueue (enqueue, get, enqueuer, close), jobRegistry
src/inline.ts     inlineBackend (wait or background, retries, backoff, retention)
src/fallback.ts   fallbackBackend (primary when available, else fallback)
src/bullmq.ts     "/bullmq" entry: bullmqBackend, startWorker, redisConnection, redisReady, bullJobOptions
scripts/test.ts   definitions, data rules, inline, fallback, enqueuer; the same scenario on inline and BullMQ (real Redis)
```

## Rules

1. **Every backend behaves the same.** Data and results cross JSON everywhere; retries, backoff,
   states, attempt counts and error messages match. Change behaviour in one backend → change it in
   all, and keep the shared scenario in `scripts/test.ts` passing on inline *and* BullMQ.
2. **Failures are safe to show.** Only a `JobFailure`'s message reaches `JobInfo.error`; every other
   error goes to `onError` and reads "Job failed". All attempts go through `runAttempt`.
3. **Payloads carry ids, never secrets.** `SECRET_KEY` keys are refused in the caller; do not loosen it
   by default. Jobs whose data must not linger use `keepResultsMs: 0`.
4. **Checks happen in the caller** (`prepareJob`): bad data fails the request, not the worker.
5. **Zero runtime dependencies in the main entry.** Only `src/bullmq.ts` imports `bullmq`/`ioredis`
   (optional peers); CI greps `dist/index.js` for it.
6. Job ids are random UUIDs; `get` returns a job only under its own definition. Ownership checks
   belong to the caller (the api's services).
7. Error codes (`WorkerError.code`) and state names (`JobState`) are public: add, never rename.
8. Backends are structural (`JobBackend`); prefer that over new options when adding a queue technology.
9. Never commit secrets, `.env` files or patient data. Tests use fictional values.

## Commands

```bash
npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run build
npm run llms      # regenerate llms-full.txt (CI fails when it is stale)
```

`npm test` needs Redis for the BullMQ part: `REDIS_URL`, or a local `redis-server` (started on a free
port). CI runs a Redis service with `REQUIRE_REDIS=1`.

## Repository rules

`main` takes pull requests only: squash merge, 1 code-owner review (`@BackStacked`), the `ci` check
required. Rules come from `mgpl-diagnostics/.github` (`scripts/protect-repos.mjs`).

## Licence

All rights reserved (see LICENSE).

## File: llms.txt

# @mgpl-diagnostics/worker-kit

> Background jobs for the MGPL Diagnostics backend (Node.js ≥ 20). Typed job definitions and one queue API over BullMQ on Redis, in-process, or worker-when-available-else-standalone; plus the worker runner. The main entry has no runtime dependencies; bullmq and ioredis are optional peers used only by "/bullmq".

Key facts for agents:
- `defineJob({ name, queue?, process(data, ctx), validate?, attempts = 3, backoffMs = 2000, keepResultsMs = 1h, keepFailedMs, maxBytes, refuseSecrets = true })`.
- `createJobQueue({ backend, jobs })` → `enqueue(job, data, { delayMs? })`, `get(job, id)`, `enqueuer(job)` (mail-kit MailQueue shape), `available()`, `close()`.
- Backends: `inlineBackend({ wait?, onError? })`, `fallbackBackend({ primary, fallback, whenFails?, onFallback? })`, and from "/bullmq" `bullmqBackend({ connection | redisUrl, prefix = "mgpl" })`.
- Worker: `startWorker({ jobs, connection | redisUrl, prefix, concurrency = 4, queues?, onError?, onFailed? })` → `{ queues, workers, close() }`.
- `JobFailure(message, retry = true)`: message shown to clients; `retry: false` fails at once. Other errors → "Job failed" + `onError`.
- `JobInfo`: id, name, queue, state (waiting | delayed | active | completed | failed), attempts, error, result, data, createdAt, finishedAt.
- Errors: `WorkerError.code` = WORKER_UNKNOWN_JOB, WORKER_BAD_DATA, WORKER_DUPLICATE_JOB, WORKER_UNAVAILABLE, WORKER_CLOSED.

## Docs

- [README](README.md): usage, backends, worker, mail-kit
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): map and rules

## Source

- [src/define.ts](src/define.ts): definitions, data checks, one attempt
- [src/queue.ts](src/queue.ts): the producer API
- [src/inline.ts](src/inline.ts): in-process backend
- [src/fallback.ts](src/fallback.ts): worker or standalone
- [src/bullmq.ts](src/bullmq.ts): BullMQ backend and worker

## File: scripts/llms-full.mjs

````js
// Builds llms-full.txt: every doc and source file of the repo in one plain-text document for AI tools.
//   node scripts/llms-full.mjs "<title>" <file-or-folder> [file-or-folder …]
// Folders are walked recursively. Output order: README, AGENTS, docs, then the rest alphabetically.
// Skipped: build output, dependencies, lockfiles, generated files, binaries. Files over 150 KB are
// listed (path + size) instead of inlined. CI checks the file is up to date (`npm run llms` + git diff).
import { readdirSync, readFileSync, statSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { extname, join, relative } from "node:path";

const [title, ...inputs] = process.argv.slice(2);
if (!title || !inputs.length) {
  console.error('usage: node scripts/llms-full.mjs "<title>" <file-or-folder> …');
  process.exit(1);
}

const TEXT = new Set([".ts", ".tsx", ".mts", ".cts", ".js", ".mjs", ".cjs", ".md", ".mdx", ".json", ".css", ".yml", ".yaml", ".txt", ".graphql", ".gql", ".sql", ".html"]);
const SKIP_DIRS = new Set(["node_modules", "dist", ".next", ".git", ".turbo", "coverage", "examples", ".pg-test"]);
const SKIP_FILES = /(^|\/)(package-lock\.json|pnpm-lock\.yaml|yarn\.lock|llms-full\.txt|[^/]*\.generated\.[^/]+|[^/]*\.log)$/;
const MAX = 150 * 1024;
const LANG = { ".ts": "ts", ".tsx": "tsx", ".mts": "ts", ".cts": "ts", ".js": "js", ".mjs": "js", ".cjs": "js", ".json": "json", ".css": "css", ".yml": "yaml", ".yaml": "yaml", ".graphql": "graphql", ".gql": "graphql", ".sql": "sql", ".html": "html" };

const posix = (p) => p.split("\\").join("/");
const files = new Set();
function walk(p) {
  const st = statSync(p);
  if (st.isDirectory()) {
    for (const name of readdirSync(p)) if (!SKIP_DIRS.has(name)) walk(join(p, name));
  } else if (TEXT.has(extname(p).toLowerCase()) && !SKIP_FILES.test(posix(p))) {
    files.add(posix(relative(".", p)));
  }
}
for (const input of inputs) walk(input);

const rank = (f) => (/^README\.md$/i.test(f) ? 0 : /^AGENTS\.md$/i.test(f) ? 1 : /^docs\//.test(f) ? 2 : 3);
const ordered = [...files].sort((a, b) => rank(a) - rank(b) || (a < b ? -1 : a > b ? 1 : 0));

const parts = [`# ${title} — full documentation and source\n\n> Generated by scripts/llms-full.mjs. Do not edit by hand. ${ordered.length} files.\n\n## Contents\n\n${ordered.map((f) => `- ${f}`).join("\n")}\n`];
const omitted = [];
for (const f of ordered) {
  // LF-normalised text, so Windows and Linux checkouts produce byte-identical output
  const body = readFileSync(f, "utf8").replace(/\r\n/g, "\n").trim();
  const size = Buffer.byteLength(body);
  if (size > MAX) {
    omitted.push(`${f} (${(size / 1024).toFixed(0)} KB)`);
    parts.push(`\n\n---\n\n## File: ${f}\n\n_Omitted: ${(size / 1024).toFixed(0)} KB. Read the file directly._\n`);
    continue;
  }
  const lang = LANG[extname(f).toLowerCase()];
  const fence = body.includes("```") ? "````" : "```";
  parts.push(`\n\n---\n\n## File: ${f}\n\n${lang ? `${fence}${lang}\n${body}\n${fence}` : body}\n`);
}
const out = parts.join("");
writeFileSync("llms-full.txt", out);
console.log(`llms-full.txt: ${ordered.length} files, ${(out.length / 1024).toFixed(0)} KB${omitted.length ? `; omitted (too large): ${omitted.join(", ")}` : ""}`);
````

## File: scripts/test.ts

```ts
// worker-kit checks: definitions, data rules, the in-process backend, fallback, the producer API,
// and BullMQ on a real Redis, where the same scenario must give the same results as in-process.
// Redis: REDIS_URL, or a local `redis-server` started here; CI sets REQUIRE_REDIS=1 so it never skips.
import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import { spawn, spawnSync, type ChildProcess } from "node:child_process";
import { createServer } from "node:net";
import { Queue } from "bullmq";
import { Redis } from "ioredis";
import { bullJobOptions, bullmqBackend, redisConnection, startWorker } from "../src/bullmq";
import {
  createJobQueue,
  defineJob,
  fallbackBackend,
  inlineBackend,
  isJobFailure,
  JobFailure,
  prepareJob,
  WorkerError,
  type AnyJob,
  type JobBackend,
  type JobContext,
  type JobInfo,
} from "../src/index";

let passed = 0;
const failures: string[] = [];
async function check(name: string, fn: () => unknown): Promise<void> {
  try {
    await fn();
    passed++;
  } catch (e) {
    failures.push(`✗ ${name}\n    ${(e as Error).stack?.split("\n").slice(0, 4).join("\n    ")}`);
  }
}
const code = async (fn: () => unknown, expected: string) => {
  try {
    await fn();
  } catch (e) {
    assert.ok(e instanceof WorkerError, `expected WorkerError, got ${String(e)}`);
    assert.equal(e.code, expected, e.message);
    return e.message;
  }
  assert.fail(`expected ${expected}`);
};
const sleep = (ms: number) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms));
async function waitFor<T>(fn: () => Promise<T | null | undefined | false>, ms = 10_000): Promise<T> {
  const end = Date.now() + ms;
  for (;;) {
    const v = await fn();
    if (v) return v;
    if (Date.now() > end) assert.fail("timed out");
    await sleep(20);
  }
}
const quiet = () => undefined;

// ---- the scenario every backend must run identically --------------------------------------------

interface SumData {
  a: number;
  b: number;
  at: Date | string;
}
function scenario() {
  const errors: string[] = [];
  const calls: Record<string, number[]> = {};
  const seen = (ctx: JobContext) => (calls[ctx.name] ??= []).push(ctx.attempt);
  const jobs = {
    sum: defineJob<SumData, { sum: number; at: unknown; when: Date }>({
      name: "sum",
      queue: "maths",
      process: (d, ctx) => {
        seen(ctx);
        return { sum: d.a + d.b, at: d.at, when: new Date(0) };
      },
    }),
    flaky: defineJob<{ n: number }, string>({
      name: "flaky",
      queue: "maths",
      attempts: 3,
      backoffMs: 10,
      process: (d, ctx) => {
        seen(ctx);
        if (ctx.attempt < 3) throw new JobFailure("Busy, try again", true);
        return `ok ${d.n} on ${ctx.attempt}/${ctx.attempts}`;
      },
    }),
    fatal: defineJob<{ invoiceId: string }, never>({
      name: "fatal",
      attempts: 5,
      backoffMs: 10,
      process: (d, ctx) => {
        seen(ctx);
        throw new JobFailure(`No invoice ${d.invoiceId}`, false);
      },
    }),
    crash: defineJob<{ id: string }, never>({
      name: "crash",
      attempts: 2,
      backoffMs: 10,
      process: (_d, ctx) => {
        seen(ctx);
        throw new Error("connect ECONNREFUSED db.internal:5432 user=admin");
      },
    }),
  };
  const onError = (e: unknown) => errors.push((e as Error).message);
  return { jobs, list: Object.values(jobs) as AnyJob[], errors, calls, onError };
}

/** Runs the scenario on a backend; returns comparable results. */
async function runScenario(backend: JobBackend, s: ReturnType<typeof scenario>) {
  const q = createJobQueue({ backend, jobs: s.list });
  const started = [
    await q.enqueue(s.jobs.sum, { a: 2, b: 3, at: new Date("2026-10-14T10:00:00.000Z") }),
    await q.enqueue(s.jobs.flaky, { n: 7 }),
    await q.enqueue(s.jobs.fatal, { invoiceId: "INV-1" }),
    await q.enqueue(s.jobs.crash, { id: "x" }),
  ];
  const done: JobInfo[] = [];
  for (const j of started) {
    const def = q.definition(j.name);
    done.push(await waitFor(async () => {
      const info = await q.get(def, j.id);
      return info && (info.state === "completed" || info.state === "failed") ? info : null;
    }));
  }
  return { q, done: done.map(({ id: _id, createdAt, finishedAt, ...rest }) => ({ ...rest, timed: createdAt instanceof Date && finishedAt instanceof Date && finishedAt >= createdAt })) };
}

const expected = [
  { name: "sum", queue: "maths", state: "completed", attempts: 1, error: null, result: { sum: 5, at: "2026-10-14T10:00:00.000Z", when: "1970-01-01T00:00:00.000Z" }, data: { a: 2, b: 3, at: "2026-10-14T10:00:00.000Z" }, timed: true },
  { name: "flaky", queue: "maths", state: "completed", attempts: 3, error: null, result: "ok 7 on 3/3", data: { n: 7 }, timed: true },
  { name: "fatal", queue: "fatal", state: "failed", attempts: 1, error: "No invoice INV-1", result: null, data: { invoiceId: "INV-1" }, timed: true },
  { name: "crash", queue: "crash", state: "failed", attempts: 2, error: "Job failed", result: null, data: { id: "x" }, timed: true },
];

// ---- definitions and data rules -----------------------------------------------------------------

await check("defineJob: defaults, queue = name, frozen", () => {
  const j = defineJob({ name: "mail", process: () => 1 });
  assert.equal(j.queue, "mail");
  assert.equal(j.attempts, 3);
  assert.equal(j.backoffMs, 2000);
  assert.equal(j.keepResultsMs, 3600_000);
  assert.equal(j.keepFailedMs, 86_400_000);
  assert.equal(j.refuseSecrets, true);
  assert.ok(Object.isFrozen(j));
  assert.equal(defineJob({ name: "x", keepResultsMs: 2 * 86_400_000, process: () => 1 }).keepFailedMs, 2 * 86_400_000);
  assert.equal(defineJob({ name: "x", attempts: 0, process: () => 1 }).attempts, 1);
});

await check("defineJob: names are checked (they become Redis keys)", async () => {
  await code(() => defineJob({ name: "Bad Name", process: () => 1 }), "WORKER_BAD_DATA");
  await code(() => defineJob({ name: "ok", queue: "a:b", process: () => 1 }), "WORKER_BAD_DATA");
  await code(() => defineJob({ name: "", process: () => 1 }), "WORKER_BAD_DATA");
});

await check("data crosses JSON: Dates become ISO strings, undefined keys drop", () => {
  const j = defineJob<Record<string, unknown>, null>({ name: "j", process: () => null });
  assert.deepEqual(prepareJob(j, { at: new Date(0), gone: undefined, n: 1 }).data, { at: "1970-01-01T00:00:00.000Z", n: 1 });
});

await check("data that is not JSON, too large, or carries secrets is refused in the caller", async () => {
  const j = defineJob<unknown, null>({ name: "j", maxBytes: 100, process: () => null });
  await code(() => prepareJob(j, { n: 1n }), "WORKER_BAD_DATA");
  await code(() => prepareJob(j, undefined), "WORKER_BAD_DATA");
  const cyclic: Record<string, unknown> = {};
  cyclic.self = cyclic;
  await code(() => prepareJob(j, cyclic), "WORKER_BAD_DATA");
  await code(() => prepareJob(j, { s: "x".repeat(200) }), "WORKER_BAD_DATA");
  const m = await code(() => prepareJob(j, { user: { id: "u1", resetToken: "abc" } }), "WORKER_BAD_DATA");
  assert.match(m, /user\.resetToken/);
  assert.doesNotMatch(m, /abc/);
  await code(() => prepareJob(j, { list: [{ PASSWORD: "x" }] }), "WORKER_BAD_DATA");
  await code(() => prepareJob(j, { headers: { authorization: "Bearer x" } }), "WORKER_BAD_DATA");
  // ids and links are fine; opting out is explicit
  prepareJob(j, { userId: "u1", tokenId: "t1", link: "https://x.example/r" });
  prepareJob(defineJob<unknown, null>({ name: "k", refuseSecrets: false, process: () => null }), { token: "x" });
});

await check("validate() runs before enqueueing; its error becomes WORKER_BAD_DATA", async () => {
  let ran = false;
  const j = defineJob<{ email: string }, null>({
    name: "j",
    validate: (d) => {
      if (!d.email.includes("@")) throw new Error("email is not valid");
    },
    process: () => {
      ran = true;
      return null;
    },
  });
  const q = createJobQueue({ backend: inlineBackend(), jobs: [j] });
  assert.match(await code(() => q.enqueue(j, { email: "nope" }), "WORKER_BAD_DATA"), /email is not valid/);
  assert.equal(ran, false);
  assert.equal((await q.enqueue(j, { email: "a@example.com" })).state, "completed");
});

await check("every job id is a fresh UUID", () => {
  const j = defineJob({ name: "j", process: () => 1 });
  const ids = new Set(Array.from({ length: 50 }, () => prepareJob(j, {}).id));
  assert.equal(ids.size, 50);
  for (const id of ids) assert.match(id, /^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-4[0-9a-f]{3}-[89ab][0-9a-f]{3}-[0-9a-f]{12}$/);
});

await check("JobFailure is recognised across package copies", () => {
  const foreign = Object.assign(new Error("x"), { name: "JobFailure", retry: false });
  assert.ok(isJobFailure(foreign));
  assert.ok(isJobFailure(new JobFailure("y")));
  assert.equal(new JobFailure("y").retry, true);
  assert.ok(!isJobFailure(new Error("z")));
});

// ---- the producer API ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

await check("createJobQueue: unknown jobs, duplicate names, foreign definitions", async () => {
  const a = defineJob({ name: "a", process: () => 1 });
  await code(() => createJobQueue({ backend: inlineBackend(), jobs: [a, defineJob({ name: "a", process: () => 2 })] }), "WORKER_DUPLICATE_JOB");
  const q = createJobQueue({ backend: inlineBackend(), jobs: [a] });
  assert.deepEqual(q.names(), ["a"]);
  assert.equal(q.mode, "inline");
  await code(() => q.enqueue("b", {}), "WORKER_UNKNOWN_JOB");
  await code(() => q.enqueue(defineJob({ name: "a", process: () => 3 }), {}), "WORKER_UNKNOWN_JOB");
  assert.equal((await q.enqueue("a", {})).result, 1);
  assert.equal(await q.get(a, ""), null);
});

await check("get only returns a job under its own definition", async () => {
  const a = defineJob({ name: "a", queue: "shared", process: () => "A" });
  const b = defineJob({ name: "b", queue: "shared", process: () => "B" });
  const q = createJobQueue({ backend: inlineBackend(), jobs: [a, b] });
  const job = await q.enqueue(a, {});
  assert.equal((await q.get(a, job.id))?.result, "A");
  assert.equal(await q.get(b, job.id), null);
  assert.equal(await q.get(a, "00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000000"), null);
});

await check("close: enqueue refused afterwards, available() false", async () => {
  const a = defineJob({ name: "a", process: () => 1 });
  const q = createJobQueue({ backend: inlineBackend(), jobs: [a] });
  assert.equal(await q.available(), true);
  await q.close();
  await q.close();
  assert.equal(await q.available(), false);
  await code(() => q.enqueue(a, {}), "WORKER_CLOSED");
});

// ---- in-process ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------

await check("inline (waiting): the scenario", async () => {
  const s = scenario();
  const { done } = await runScenario(inlineBackend({ onError: s.onError }), s);
  assert.deepEqual(done, expected);
  assert.deepEqual(s.calls, { sum: [1], flaky: [1, 2, 3], fatal: [1], crash: [1, 2] });
  assert.equal(s.errors.length, 2);
});

await check("inline (background): the scenario, with backoff between attempts", async () => {
  const s = scenario();
  const t0 = Date.now();
  const { done } = await runScenario(inlineBackend({ wait: false, onError: s.onError }), s);
  assert.deepEqual(done, expected);
  assert.ok(Date.now() - t0 >= 30, "flaky waited 10 + 20 ms");
});

await check("inline (background): add resolves before the job runs", async () => {
  let release!: () => void;
  const gate = new Promise<void>((r) => (release = r));
  const j = defineJob({ name: "slow", process: async () => (await gate, "done") });
  const q = createJobQueue({ backend: inlineBackend({ wait: false }), jobs: [j] });
  const info = await q.enqueue(j, {});
  assert.equal(info.state, "waiting");
  await sleep(5);
  assert.equal((await q.get(j, info.id))?.state, "active");
  release();
  assert.equal((await waitFor(async () => ((await q.get(j, info.id))?.state === "completed" ? q.get(j, info.id) : null)))?.result, "done");
});

await check("inline: errors that are not JobFailure are hidden and passed to onError", async () => {
  const logged: unknown[] = [];
  const j = defineJob({ name: "j", attempts: 1, process: () => Promise.reject(new Error("secret internals")) });
  const q = createJobQueue({ backend: inlineBackend({ onError: (e, ctx) => logged.push([(e as Error).message, ctx.name, ctx.attempt]) }), jobs: [j] });
  const info = await q.enqueue(j, {});
  assert.equal(info.state, "failed");
  assert.equal(info.error, "Job failed");
  assert.deepEqual(logged, [["secret internals", "j", 1]]);
});

await check("inline: a result that is not JSON fails without retrying", async () => {
  let runs = 0;
  const j = defineJob({ name: "j", process: () => (runs++, { n: 1n }) });
  const info = await createJobQueue({ backend: inlineBackend({ onError: quiet }), jobs: [j] }).enqueue(j, {});
  assert.equal(info.state, "failed");
  assert.equal(runs, 1);
});

await check("inline: delayed jobs wait, then run", async () => {
  const j = defineJob({ name: "later", process: () => "ran" });
  const q = createJobQueue({ backend: inlineBackend(), jobs: [j] });
  const info = await q.enqueue(j, {}, { delayMs: 40 });
  assert.equal(info.state, "delayed");
  await sleep(10);
  assert.equal((await q.get(j, info.id))?.state, "delayed");
  const done = await waitFor(async () => ((await q.get(j, info.id))?.state === "completed" ? q.get(j, info.id) : null));
  assert.equal(done?.result, "ran");
});

await check("inline: results are kept for keepResultsMs, failures for keepFailedMs", async () => {
  const gone = defineJob({ name: "gone", keepResultsMs: 0, process: () => "x" });
  const brief = defineJob({ name: "brief", keepResultsMs: 30, process: () => "y" });
  const bad = defineJob({ name: "bad", attempts: 1, keepFailedMs: 30, process: () => Promise.reject(new JobFailure("no", false)) });
  const q = createJobQueue({ backend: inlineBackend(), jobs: [gone, brief, bad] });
  const g = await q.enqueue(gone, {});
  assert.equal(g.result, "x", "the caller still sees the outcome");
  assert.equal(await q.get(gone, g.id), null);
  const b = await q.enqueue(brief, {});
  const f = await q.enqueue(bad, {});
  assert.equal((await q.get(brief, b.id))?.result, "y");
  assert.equal((await q.get(bad, f.id))?.error, "no");
  await sleep(40);
  assert.equal(await q.get(brief, b.id), null);
  assert.equal(await q.get(bad, f.id), null);
});

await check("inline: close finishes jobs in hand and drops pending delays", async () => {
  let finished = false;
  let delayedRan = false;
  const slow = defineJob({ name: "slow", process: async () => (await sleep(30), (finished = true)) });
  const later = defineJob({ name: "later", process: () => (delayedRan = true) });
  const q = createJobQueue({ backend: inlineBackend({ wait: false }), jobs: [slow, later] });
  await q.enqueue(slow, {});
  await q.enqueue(later, {}, { delayMs: 60_000 });
  await sleep(5);
  const t0 = Date.now();
  await q.close();
  assert.ok(finished);
  assert.ok(!delayedRan);
  assert.ok(Date.now() - t0 < 1000, "did not wait for the delay");
});

// ---- fallback -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

function fakeBackend(o: { available?: boolean; fails?: boolean }) {
  const added: string[] = [];
  const inner = inlineBackend();
  const b: JobBackend = {
    mode: "fake",
    async add(job) {
      if (o.fails) throw new Error("redis went away");
      added.push(job.def.name);
      return inner.add(job);
    },
    get: (def, id) => inner.get(def, id),
    available: () => o.available ?? true,
    close: () => inner.close(),
  };
  return { b, added };
}

await check("fallback: the primary when available", async () => {
  const p = fakeBackend({});
  const fellBack: unknown[] = [];
  const j = defineJob({ name: "j", process: () => 1 });
  const q = createJobQueue({ backend: fallbackBackend({ primary: p.b, fallback: inlineBackend(), onFallback: (r) => fellBack.push(r) }), jobs: [j] });
  const info = await q.enqueue(j, {});
  assert.deepEqual(p.added, ["j"]);
  assert.equal(fellBack.length, 0);
  assert.equal((await q.get(j, info.id))?.result, 1);
  assert.equal(q.mode, "fallback");
});

await check("fallback: standalone when the primary is unavailable or fails", async () => {
  for (const o of [{ available: false }, { fails: true }]) {
    const p = fakeBackend(o);
    const reasons: string[] = [];
    const j = defineJob({ name: "j", process: () => 2 });
    const q = createJobQueue({ backend: fallbackBackend({ primary: p.b, fallback: inlineBackend(), onFallback: (r) => reasons.push((r as Error).message) }), jobs: [j] });
    const info = await q.enqueue(j, {});
    assert.equal(info.result, 2);
    assert.deepEqual(p.added, []);
    assert.equal(reasons.length, 1);
    assert.equal((await q.get(j, info.id))?.result, 2, "found on the fallback");
    assert.equal(await q.available(), true);
  }
});

await check("fallback: whenFails 'throw' raises WORKER_UNAVAILABLE", async () => {
  const j = defineJob({ name: "j", process: () => 1 });
  for (const o of [{ available: false }, { fails: true }]) {
    const q = createJobQueue({ backend: fallbackBackend({ primary: fakeBackend(o).b, fallback: inlineBackend(), whenFails: "throw" }), jobs: [j] });
    await code(() => q.enqueue(j, {}), "WORKER_UNAVAILABLE");
  }
});

await check("enqueuer: mail-kit's MailQueue shape", async () => {
  // mail-kit: interface MailQueue { enqueue(job): Promise<string | undefined>; available?(): boolean | Promise<boolean> }
  interface MailQueueShape {
    enqueue(job: { v: 1; template: string }): Promise<string | undefined>;
    available?(): boolean | Promise<boolean>;
  }
  const sent: string[] = [];
  const mail = defineJob<{ v: 1; template: string }, null>({ name: "mail", keepResultsMs: 0, process: (d) => (sent.push(d.template), null) });
  const broken = defineJob<{ v: 1; template: string }, null>({ name: "broken", attempts: 1, process: () => Promise.reject(new JobFailure("SMTP refused", false)) });
  const q = createJobQueue({ backend: inlineBackend(), jobs: [mail, broken] });
  const mq: MailQueueShape = q.enqueuer(mail);
  const id = await mq.enqueue({ v: 1, template: "password-reset" });
  assert.equal(typeof id, "string");
  assert.deepEqual(sent, ["password-reset"]);
  assert.equal(await mq.available?.(), true);
  await assert.rejects(q.enqueuer(broken).enqueue({ v: 1, template: "x" }), /SMTP refused/);
});

// ---- BullMQ on Redis ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

async function freePort(): Promise<number> {
  return new Promise((resolve) => {
    const s = createServer().listen(0, "127.0.0.1", () => {
      const port = (s.address() as { port: number }).port;
      s.close(() => resolve(port));
    });
  });
}

let redisUrl = process.env.REDIS_URL;
let redisServer: ChildProcess | undefined;
if (!redisUrl && spawnSync("redis-server", ["--version"]).status === 0) {
  const port = await freePort();
  redisServer = spawn("redis-server", ["--port", String(port), "--save", "", "--appendonly", "no"], { stdio: "ignore" });
  redisUrl = `redis://127.0.0.1:${port}`;
  const probe = new Redis(redisUrl, { lazyConnect: true, maxRetriesPerRequest: 0, retryStrategy: () => 50 });
  probe.on("error", quiet);
  await waitFor(async () => (await probe.connect().then(() => true, () => false)) && (await probe.ping()) === "PONG", 5000);
  probe.disconnect();
}

if (!redisUrl) {
  if (process.env.REQUIRE_REDIS) failures.push("✗ BullMQ checks: no Redis (set REDIS_URL or install redis-server)");
  else console.log("- BullMQ checks skipped: no REDIS_URL and no redis-server");
} else {
  const prefix = `wk-test-${process.pid}`;
  const admin = new Redis(redisUrl);

  await check("bullmq: the scenario gives the same results as in-process", async () => {
    const s = scenario();
    const worker = startWorker({ redisUrl, prefix, jobs: s.list, concurrency: 2, onError: s.onError, onFailed: quiet });
    assert.deepEqual(worker.queues.sort(), ["crash", "fatal", "maths"]);
    const backend = bullmqBackend({ redisUrl, prefix });
    await waitFor(async () => backend.available?.());
    const { q, done } = await runScenario(backend, s);
    assert.equal(q.mode, "bullmq");
    assert.deepEqual(done, expected);
    assert.deepEqual(s.calls, { sum: [1], flaky: [1, 2, 3], fatal: [1], crash: [1, 2] });
    assert.equal(s.errors.length, 2);
    await worker.close();
    await q.close();
  });

  await check("bullmq: keys use the prefix and queue; job options come from the definition", async () => {
    const j = defineJob({ name: "keys", queue: "kq", attempts: 4, backoffMs: 500, keepResultsMs: 60_000, keepFailedMs: 120_000, process: () => 1 });
    const prepared = prepareJob(j, { id: "a" }, { delayMs: 1000 });
    assert.deepEqual(bullJobOptions(prepared), { jobId: prepared.id, attempts: 4, backoff: { type: "exponential", delay: 500 }, delay: 1000, removeOnComplete: { age: 60 }, removeOnFail: { age: 120 } });
    const q = createJobQueue({ backend: bullmqBackend({ redisUrl, prefix }), jobs: [j] });
    const info = await q.enqueue(j, { id: "a" }, { delayMs: 60_000 });
    assert.equal(info.state, "delayed");
    assert.equal((await q.get(j, info.id))?.state, "delayed");
    assert.ok((await admin.keys(`${prefix}:kq:*`)).length > 0);
    await q.close();
  });

  await check("bullmq: keepResultsMs 0 removes the job (and its data) once done", async () => {
    const j = defineJob({ name: "mail", keepResultsMs: 0, process: () => "sent" });
    const worker = startWorker({ redisUrl, prefix, jobs: [j] });
    const q = createJobQueue({ backend: bullmqBackend({ redisUrl, prefix }), jobs: [j] });
    const info = await q.enqueue(j, { link: "https://x.example/reset/abc" });
    await waitFor(async () => (await q.get(j, info.id)) === null);
    assert.equal(await admin.exists(`${prefix}:mail:${info.id}`), 0);
    await worker.close();
    await q.close();
  });

  await check("bullmq: get under another definition returns null", async () => {
    const a = defineJob({ name: "a", queue: "same", process: () => 1 });
    const b = defineJob({ name: "b", queue: "same", process: () => 2 });
    const q = createJobQueue({ backend: bullmqBackend({ redisUrl, prefix }), jobs: [a, b] });
    const info = await q.enqueue(a, {}, { delayMs: 60_000 });
    assert.equal((await q.get(a, info.id))?.name, "a");
    assert.equal(await q.get(b, info.id), null);
    await q.close();
  });

  await check("bullmq: a job name the worker does not know fails at once", async () => {
    const known = defineJob({ name: "known", queue: "mixed", process: () => 1 });
    const failed: { name: string; final: boolean }[] = [];
    const worker = startWorker({ redisUrl, prefix, jobs: [known], onFailed: (f) => failed.push(f) });
    const raw = new Queue("mixed", { connection: redisConnection(redisUrl), prefix });
    await raw.add("stranger", {}, { attempts: 3 });
    await waitFor(async () => failed.length > 0);
    assert.deepEqual(failed.map((f) => [f.name, f.final]), [["stranger", true]]);
    await raw.close();
    await worker.close();
  });

  await check("bullmq: a shared connection is not closed by worker-kit", async () => {
    const connection = redisConnection(redisUrl);
    const j = defineJob({ name: "shared", process: () => "x" });
    const worker = startWorker({ connection, prefix, jobs: [j] });
    const q = createJobQueue({ backend: bullmqBackend({ connection, prefix }), jobs: [j] });
    const info = await q.enqueue(j, {});
    await waitFor(async () => (await q.get(j, info.id))?.state === "completed");
    await worker.close();
    await q.close();
    assert.equal(await connection.ping(), "PONG");
    await connection.quit();
  });

  await check("bullmq + fallback: Redis down → jobs run standalone, without waiting", async () => {
    const port = await freePort(); // nothing listens here
    const down = new Redis(`redis://127.0.0.1:${port}`, { maxRetriesPerRequest: null, lazyConnect: true });
    down.on("error", quiet);
    const ran: string[] = [];
    const j = defineJob<{ to: string }, null>({ name: "mail", process: (d) => (ran.push(d.to), null) });
    const reasons: string[] = [];
    const q = createJobQueue({
      backend: fallbackBackend({ primary: bullmqBackend({ connection: down, prefix }), fallback: inlineBackend(), onFallback: (r) => reasons.push((r as Error).message) }),
      jobs: [j],
    });
    const t0 = Date.now();
    const info = await q.enqueue(j, { to: "a@example.com" });
    assert.ok(Date.now() - t0 < 1000);
    assert.equal(info.state, "completed");
    assert.deepEqual(ran, ["a@example.com"]);
    assert.match(reasons[0] ?? "", /bullmq backend is not available/);
    await q.close();
    down.disconnect();
  });

  await check("bullmq: needs a connection or a URL", async () => {
    await code(() => bullmqBackend({}), "WORKER_UNAVAILABLE");
  });

  const leftovers = await admin.keys(`${prefix}:*`);
  if (leftovers.length) await admin.del(...leftovers);
  await admin.quit();
}
redisServer?.kill();

for (const f of failures) console.log(f);
console.log(`\n${passed} passed, ${failures.length} failed`);
process.exit(failures.length ? 1 : 0);
```


---

## File: src/bullmq.ts

```ts
// "/bullmq" entry: the BullMQ-on-Redis backend (producer) and the worker runner (consumer).
// bullmq and ioredis are optional peers; nothing else in the package imports them.
import { Job, Queue, UnrecoverableError, Worker, type ConnectionOptions, type JobsOptions } from "bullmq";
import { Redis } from "ioredis";
import { logError, runAttempt, type ErrorHandler } from "./define";
import { isJobFailure, WorkerError } from "./errors";
import { jobRegistry } from "./queue";
import type { AnyJob, JobBackend, JobInfo, JobState, PreparedJob } from "./types";

export interface RedisOptions {
  /** An ioredis connection you own (not closed by worker-kit). Give this or `redisUrl`. */
  connection?: Redis;
  /** worker-kit opens (and closes) its own connection. */
  redisUrl?: string;
  /** Redis key prefix: keys are `<prefix>:<queue>:…`. Default "mgpl". */
  prefix?: string;
}

/** An ioredis connection as BullMQ needs it (`maxRetriesPerRequest: null` for blocking commands). */
export function redisConnection(url: string): Redis {
  return new Redis(url, { maxRetriesPerRequest: null });
}

/** `available` check for a connection: true only while it is "ready" (ioredis would otherwise queue commands while down). */
export const redisReady = (connection: Redis) => () => connection.status === "ready";

function own(o: RedisOptions): { connection: Redis; owned: boolean } {
  if (o.connection) return { connection: o.connection, owned: false };
  if (o.redisUrl) {
    const connection = redisConnection(o.redisUrl);
    // ioredis reconnects by itself; `available()` reports the outage. Without a listener every retry is printed.
    connection.on("error", () => undefined);
    return { connection, owned: true };
  }
  throw new WorkerError("WORKER_UNAVAILABLE", "Give a Redis `connection` or a `redisUrl`");
}

const seconds = (ms: number) => Math.max(1, Math.ceil(ms / 1000));

/** BullMQ job options from a definition: the only place they are set. */
export function bullJobOptions(job: PreparedJob): JobsOptions {
  const { def } = job;
  return {
    jobId: job.id,
    attempts: def.attempts,
    backoff: { type: "exponential", delay: def.backoffMs },
    ...(job.delayMs > 0 ? { delay: job.delayMs } : {}),
    removeOnComplete: def.keepResultsMs === 0 ? true : { age: seconds(def.keepResultsMs) },
    removeOnFail: def.keepFailedMs === 0 ? true : { age: seconds(def.keepFailedMs) },
  };
}

const STATES: Record<string, JobState> = { waiting: "waiting", "waiting-children": "waiting", prioritized: "waiting", active: "active", completed: "completed", failed: "failed", delayed: "delayed" };

async function toInfo(job: Job, queue: string): Promise<JobInfo> {
  const state = STATES[await job.getState()] ?? "waiting";
  return {
    id: job.id!,
    name: job.name,
    queue,
    state,
    attempts: job.attemptsMade,
    error: state === "completed" ? null : job.failedReason || null,
    result: state === "completed" ? ((job.returnvalue as unknown) ?? null) : null,
    data: job.data as unknown,
    createdAt: new Date(job.timestamp),
    finishedAt: job.finishedOn && (state === "completed" || state === "failed") ? new Date(job.finishedOn) : null,
  };
}

/**
 * The producer side (API processes): adds jobs to Redis. Run `startWorker` somewhere to process them.
 * `available()` is false while the Redis connection is not "ready" (use it with fallbackBackend).
 */
export function bullmqBackend(o: RedisOptions): JobBackend {
  const { connection, owned } = own(o);
  const prefix = o.prefix ?? "mgpl";
  const queues = new Map<string, Queue>();
  const queueFor = (name: string) => {
    let q = queues.get(name);
    if (!q) {
      q = new Queue(name, { connection: connection as unknown as ConnectionOptions, prefix });
      queues.set(name, q);
    }
    return q;
  };
  return {
    mode: "bullmq",
    async add(job) {
      const added = await queueFor(job.def.queue).add(job.def.name, job.data, bullJobOptions(job));
      return toInfo(added, job.def.queue);
    },
    async get(def: AnyJob, id: string) {
      const job = await Job.fromId(queueFor(def.queue), id);
      return job && job.name === def.name ? toInfo(job, def.queue) : null;
    },
    available: redisReady(connection),
    async close() {
      await Promise.all([...queues.values()].map((q) => q.close()));
      if (owned) await connection.quit().catch(() => undefined);
    },
  };
}

export interface StartWorkerOptions extends RedisOptions {
  /** The definitions to run. One BullMQ Worker per distinct queue. */
  jobs: readonly AnyJob[];
  /** Only these queues (default: every queue of `jobs`). */
  queues?: readonly string[];
  /** Jobs a worker runs at once, per queue. Default 4. */
  concurrency?: number;
  /** Errors that are not a JobFailure (with the job context). Default: one line on stderr. */
  onError?: ErrorHandler;
  /** Each failed attempt (after onError). Default: one warning line. */
  onFailed?: (info: { id: string | undefined; name: string; queue: string; attempt: number; error: string; final: boolean }) => void;
}

export interface RunningWorker {
  queues: string[];
  workers: Worker[];
  /** Finishes the jobs in hand, then stops. */
  close(): Promise<void>;
}

/** The consumer side (`node dist/worker.js` in the api): runs the definitions' processors. */
export function startWorker(o: StartWorkerOptions): RunningWorker {
  const byName = jobRegistry(o.jobs);
  const { connection, owned } = own(o);
  const prefix = o.prefix ?? "mgpl";
  const onError = o.onError ?? logError;
  const onFailed =
    o.onFailed ?? ((f) => console.warn(`[worker-kit] ${f.queue}/${f.name} job ${f.id} failed (attempt ${f.attempt}${f.final ? ", final" : ""}): ${f.error}`));
  const names = [...new Set(o.jobs.map((j) => j.queue))].filter((q) => !o.queues || o.queues.includes(q));

  const workers = names.map((queue) => {
    const w = new Worker(
      queue,
      async (job: Job) => {
        const def = byName.get(job.name);
        if (!def || def.queue !== queue) throw new UnrecoverableError(`Unknown job "${job.name}" on queue "${queue}"`);
        const ctx = { id: job.id ?? "", name: job.name, queue, attempt: job.attemptsMade + 1, attempts: job.opts.attempts ?? def.attempts };
        try {
          return await runAttempt(def, job.data, ctx, onError);
        } catch (e) {
          const message = isJobFailure(e) ? e.message : "Job failed";
          // a JobFailure that retrying cannot fix fails the job at once
          if (isJobFailure(e) && !e.retry) throw new UnrecoverableError(message);
          throw new Error(message);
        }
      },
      { connection: connection as unknown as ConnectionOptions, prefix, concurrency: Math.max(1, o.concurrency ?? 4) },
    );
    w.on("failed", (job, err) => {
      if (!job) return;
      const final = err instanceof UnrecoverableError || err.name === "UnrecoverableError" || job.attemptsMade >= (job.opts.attempts ?? 1);
      onFailed({ id: job.id, name: job.name, queue, attempt: job.attemptsMade, error: err.message, final });
    });
    // without a listener an "error" event (e.g. Redis dropped) would crash the process
    w.on("error", (err) => console.error(`[worker-kit] ${queue} worker:`, err.message));
    return w;
  });

  return {
    queues: names,
    workers,
    async close() {
      await Promise.all(workers.map((w) => w.close()));
      if (owned) await connection.quit().catch(() => undefined);
    },
  };
}
```

## File: src/define.ts

```ts
import { randomUUID } from "node:crypto";
import { GENERIC_FAILURE, isJobFailure, JobFailure, WorkerError } from "./errors";
import type { AnyJob, EnqueueOptions, JobContext, JobDefinition, PreparedJob } from "./types";

export interface DefineJobOptions<Data, Result> {
  name: string;
  queue?: string;
  validate?: (data: Data) => void;
  process: (data: Data, ctx: JobContext) => Promise<Result> | Result;
  /** Default 3. */
  attempts?: number;
  /** First retry delay; doubles each time. Default 2 s. */
  backoffMs?: number;
  /** Default 1 hour. Use 0 for jobs whose data must not linger (e.g. a mail with a reset link). */
  keepResultsMs?: number;
  /** Default max(1 day, keepResultsMs). */
  keepFailedMs?: number;
  /** Default 512 KiB. */
  maxBytes?: number;
  /** Default true. */
  refuseSecrets?: boolean;
}

const NAME = /^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,63}$/;

/** Keys that must not appear in job data: payloads carry ids, never tokens or secrets. */
export const SECRET_KEY = /^(password|passwordhash|token|accesstoken|refreshtoken|resettoken|secret|clientsecret|apikey|api_key|authorization|cookie)$/i;

export function defineJob<Data, Result>(o: DefineJobOptions<Data, Result>): JobDefinition<Data, Result> {
  const queue = o.queue ?? o.name;
  if (!NAME.test(o.name)) throw new WorkerError("WORKER_BAD_DATA", `Job name "${o.name}" must match ${NAME}`);
  if (!NAME.test(queue)) throw new WorkerError("WORKER_BAD_DATA", `Queue name "${queue}" must match ${NAME}`);
  const attempts = Math.max(1, Math.floor(o.attempts ?? 3));
  const keepResultsMs = Math.max(0, o.keepResultsMs ?? 3600_000);
  return Object.freeze({
    name: o.name,
    queue,
    validate: o.validate,
    process: o.process,
    attempts,
    backoffMs: Math.max(0, o.backoffMs ?? 2000),
    keepResultsMs,
    keepFailedMs: Math.max(0, o.keepFailedMs ?? Math.max(86_400_000, keepResultsMs)),
    maxBytes: o.maxBytes ?? 512 * 1024,
    refuseSecrets: o.refuseSecrets ?? true,
  });
}

/** Delay before attempt `n + 1` after `n` failed attempts (exponential, the same as BullMQ's). */
export const backoffDelay = (def: AnyJob, failedAttempts: number) => def.backoffMs * 2 ** (failedAttempts - 1);

function findSecret(v: unknown, path: string, seen = 0): string | null {
  if (seen > 64 || v === null || typeof v !== "object") return null;
  if (Array.isArray(v)) {
    for (let i = 0; i < v.length; i++) {
      const hit = findSecret(v[i], `${path}[${i}]`, seen + 1);
      if (hit) return hit;
    }
    return null;
  }
  for (const [k, child] of Object.entries(v)) {
    if (SECRET_KEY.test(k)) return path ? `${path}.${k}` : k;
    const hit = findSecret(child, path ? `${path}.${k}` : k, seen + 1);
    if (hit) return hit;
  }
  return null;
}

/** JSON round trip with the definition's checks, so every backend sees exactly what Redis would hold. */
export function toJsonData(def: AnyJob, data: unknown): unknown {
  let json: string | undefined;
  try {
    json = JSON.stringify(data);
  } catch (e) {
    throw new WorkerError("WORKER_BAD_DATA", `Job "${def.name}": data is not JSON (${(e as Error).message})`);
  }
  if (json === undefined) throw new WorkerError("WORKER_BAD_DATA", `Job "${def.name}": data is not JSON`);
  const bytes = Buffer.byteLength(json);
  if (bytes > def.maxBytes) throw new WorkerError("WORKER_BAD_DATA", `Job "${def.name}": data is ${bytes} bytes, the limit is ${def.maxBytes}`);
  const parsed: unknown = JSON.parse(json);
  if (def.refuseSecrets) {
    const key = findSecret(parsed, "");
    if (key) throw new WorkerError("WORKER_BAD_DATA", `Job "${def.name}": data carries a secret-looking key "${key}"; pass an id and look the value up in the processor`);
  }
  return parsed;
}

/** Validates and serialises a job for a backend. Runs in the caller, so bad data fails the request. */
export function prepareJob(def: AnyJob, data: unknown, o: EnqueueOptions = {}): PreparedJob {
  if (def.validate) {
    try {
      def.validate(data);
    } catch (e) {
      throw e instanceof WorkerError ? e : new WorkerError("WORKER_BAD_DATA", `Job "${def.name}": ${(e as Error).message}`);
    }
  }
  return {
    id: randomUUID(), // unguessable; callers still check ownership on every read
    def,
    data: toJsonData(def, data),
    delayMs: Math.max(0, Math.floor(o.delayMs ?? 0)),
  };
}

export type ErrorHandler = (error: unknown, ctx: JobContext) => void;

/**
 * Runs one attempt. Every backend goes through here, so failures read the same everywhere:
 * a JobFailure keeps its message and retry flag; anything else goes to `onError` (log it) and
 * becomes a retryable "Job failed", so internals never reach the client.
 */
export async function runAttempt(def: AnyJob, data: unknown, ctx: JobContext, onError?: ErrorHandler): Promise<unknown> {
  let result: unknown;
  try {
    result = await def.process(data, ctx);
  } catch (e) {
    if (isJobFailure(e)) throw e;
    onError?.(e, ctx);
    throw new JobFailure(GENERIC_FAILURE, true);
  }
  if (result === undefined) return null;
  try {
    return JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(result)) as unknown;
  } catch (e) {
    onError?.(e, ctx);
    throw new JobFailure(GENERIC_FAILURE, false);
  }
}

/** The default onError: one line on stderr, without the job's data. */
export const logError: ErrorHandler = (e, ctx) => {
  console.error(`[worker-kit] ${ctx.queue}/${ctx.name} job ${ctx.id} attempt ${ctx.attempt}/${ctx.attempts} failed:`, e);
};
```

## File: src/errors.ts

```ts
/** Error codes are a public contract: add, never rename. */
export type WorkerErrorCode =
  | "WORKER_UNKNOWN_JOB" // enqueue/get/run of a job name that is not defined
  | "WORKER_BAD_DATA" // data is not JSON, too large, carries a secret key, or failed validate()
  | "WORKER_DUPLICATE_JOB" // two definitions with the same name
  | "WORKER_UNAVAILABLE" // no backend could take the job
  | "WORKER_CLOSED"; // the queue was closed

export class WorkerError extends Error {
  constructor(readonly code: WorkerErrorCode, message: string) {
    super(message);
    this.name = "WorkerError";
  }
}

/**
 * Throw from a processor for a failure whose message is safe to show to the client.
 * `retry: false` fails the job at once (retrying cannot help); `true` uses the remaining attempts.
 * Any other error is logged through `onError` and shown as "Job failed".
 */
export class JobFailure extends Error {
  constructor(message: string, readonly retry: boolean = true) {
    super(message);
    this.name = "JobFailure";
  }
}

/** True for a JobFailure, also one made by another copy of this package. */
export function isJobFailure(e: unknown): e is JobFailure {
  return e instanceof JobFailure || (e instanceof Error && e.name === "JobFailure" && typeof (e as { retry?: unknown }).retry === "boolean");
}

/** The message shown for failures that are not a JobFailure. */
export const GENERIC_FAILURE = "Job failed";
```


---

## File: src/fallback.ts

```ts
// "The worker if it is there, otherwise standalone": jobs go to the primary backend (BullMQ on
// Redis) while it is available, and run on the fallback (usually in-process) when it is not.
import { WorkerError } from "./errors";
import type { JobBackend, PreparedJob } from "./types";

export interface FallbackBackendOptions {
  primary: JobBackend;
  fallback: JobBackend;
  /** When the primary is unavailable or `add` fails: "fallback" (default) or "throw" (WORKER_UNAVAILABLE). */
  whenFails?: "fallback" | "throw";
  /** Called each time a job went to the fallback (log it). */
  onFallback?: (reason: unknown, job: PreparedJob) => void;
}

export function fallbackBackend(o: FallbackBackendOptions): JobBackend {
  const { primary, fallback } = o;
  const isAvailable = async (b: JobBackend) => {
    try {
      return (await (b.available?.() ?? true)) === true;
    } catch {
      return false;
    }
  };
  return {
    mode: "fallback",
    async add(job) {
      let reason: unknown;
      if (await isAvailable(primary)) {
        try {
          return await primary.add(job);
        } catch (e) {
          reason = e;
        }
      } else {
        reason = new WorkerError("WORKER_UNAVAILABLE", `The ${primary.mode} backend is not available`);
      }
      if (o.whenFails === "throw") {
        throw reason instanceof WorkerError ? reason : new WorkerError("WORKER_UNAVAILABLE", `Could not queue job "${job.def.name}": ${reason instanceof Error ? reason.message : String(reason)}`);
      }
      o.onFallback?.(reason, job);
      return fallback.add(job);
    },
    async get(def, id) {
      // ids are UUIDs, so a job is on one side only; a primary that is down just has nothing to say
      const fromPrimary = (await isAvailable(primary)) ? await primary.get(def, id).catch(() => null) : null;
      return fromPrimary ?? fallback.get(def, id);
    },
    async available() {
      return (await isAvailable(primary)) || (await isAvailable(fallback));
    },
    async close() {
      await Promise.all([primary.close(), fallback.close()]);
    },
  };
}
```

## File: src/inline.ts

```ts
// Jobs in this process, no Redis: development, tests, a single server, and the standalone side of
// fallbackBackend. Same definitions, same JSON data, same retries and same error messages as BullMQ.
import { backoffDelay, logError, runAttempt, type ErrorHandler } from "./define";
import { GENERIC_FAILURE, isJobFailure, WorkerError } from "./errors";
import type { AnyJob, JobBackend, JobInfo, PreparedJob } from "./types";

export interface InlineBackendOptions {
  /**
   * true (default): `add` runs the job at once and resolves when it has finished (the request waits),
   * retrying immediately. false: `add` resolves at once and the job runs in the background of this
   * process, with the definition's backoff between attempts. A delayed job always runs in the background.
   */
  wait?: boolean;
  /** Called with errors that are not a JobFailure. Default: one line on stderr. */
  onError?: ErrorHandler;
}

interface Entry {
  info: JobInfo;
  def: AnyJob;
}

export function inlineBackend(o: InlineBackendOptions = {}): JobBackend {
  const wait = o.wait ?? true;
  const onError = o.onError ?? logError;
  const jobs = new Map<string, Entry>();
  const running = new Set<Promise<void>>();
  const timers = new Map<NodeJS.Timeout, () => void>();
  let closed = false;

  const prune = () => {
    const now = Date.now();
    for (const [id, { info, def }] of jobs) {
      const finished = info.finishedAt?.getTime();
      if (finished === undefined) continue;
      const keep = info.state === "failed" ? def.keepFailedMs : def.keepResultsMs;
      if (finished + keep <= now) jobs.delete(id);
    }
  };

  const sleep = (ms: number) =>
    new Promise<void>((resolve) => {
      const t = setTimeout(() => {
        timers.delete(t);
        resolve();
      }, ms);
      timers.set(t, resolve);
    });

  /** Runs every attempt; never rejects. */
  async function run(entry: Entry, delayFirst: number, backoff: boolean): Promise<void> {
    const { info, def } = entry;
    if (delayFirst > 0) await sleep(delayFirst);
    else if (backoff) await new Promise((r) => setImmediate(r)); // background: after `add` has returned
    while (!closed) {
      info.state = "active";
      info.attempts++;
      try {
        info.result = await runAttempt(def, info.data, { id: info.id, name: info.name, queue: info.queue, attempt: info.attempts, attempts: def.attempts }, onError);
        info.state = "completed";
        info.error = null;
        break;
      } catch (e) {
        info.error = isJobFailure(e) ? e.message : GENERIC_FAILURE;
        if (!(isJobFailure(e) && e.retry) || info.attempts >= def.attempts) {
          info.state = "failed";
          break;
        }
        info.state = "delayed";
        if (backoff) await sleep(backoffDelay(def, info.attempts));
      }
    }
    if (info.state === "completed" || info.state === "failed") info.finishedAt = new Date();
  }

  const track = (p: Promise<void>) => {
    running.add(p);
    void p.finally(() => running.delete(p));
  };

  const snapshot = (info: JobInfo): JobInfo => ({ ...info });

  return {
    mode: "inline",
    async add(job: PreparedJob) {
      if (closed) throw new WorkerError("WORKER_CLOSED", "The job queue is closed");
      prune();
      const info: JobInfo = {
        id: job.id,
        name: job.def.name,
        queue: job.def.queue,
        state: job.delayMs > 0 ? "delayed" : "waiting",
        attempts: 0,
        error: null,
        result: null,
        data: job.data,
        createdAt: new Date(),
        finishedAt: null,
      };
      const entry: Entry = { info, def: job.def };
      jobs.set(info.id, entry);
      if (wait && job.delayMs === 0) {
        await run(entry, 0, false);
        const out = snapshot(info);
        prune(); // keepResultsMs 0: gone for `get`, but the caller still gets the outcome
        return out;
      }
      track(run(entry, job.delayMs, true));
      return snapshot(info);
    },
    async get(def, id) {
      prune();
      const e = jobs.get(id);
      return e && e.info.name === def.name && e.info.queue === def.queue ? snapshot(e.info) : null;
    },
    available: () => !closed,
    async close() {
      closed = true;
      // pending delays and backoffs end now; jobs not yet finished are dropped (nothing persists in-process)
      for (const [t, resolve] of timers) {
        clearTimeout(t);
        resolve();
      }
      timers.clear();
      await Promise.allSettled([...running]);
      jobs.clear();
    },
  };
}
```

## File: src/queue.ts

```ts
// The producer API: one object the app's services use to start jobs and read them back,
// whatever backend sits underneath.
import { prepareJob } from "./define";
import { WorkerError } from "./errors";
import type { AnyJob, DataOf, EnqueueOptions, JobBackend, JobInfo, ResultOf } from "./types";

export interface JobQueueOptions {
  backend: JobBackend;
  /** Every job this queue may start. Names are unique. */
  jobs: readonly AnyJob[];
}

/** A one-job producer with mail-kit's `MailQueue` shape: `createMailer({ queue: jobs.enqueuer(mailJob) })`. */
export interface Enqueuer<Data> {
  /** Starts the job; resolves with its id. Rejects when it could not be queued or (in-process) failed. */
  enqueue(data: Data): Promise<string>;
  available(): Promise<boolean>;
}

export interface JobQueue {
  readonly mode: string;
  /** Validates the data here (bad data fails the caller), then hands the job to the backend. */
  enqueue<J extends AnyJob>(job: J, data: DataOf<J>, o?: EnqueueOptions): Promise<JobInfo<DataOf<J>, ResultOf<J>>>;
  enqueue(job: string, data: unknown, o?: EnqueueOptions): Promise<JobInfo>;
  /** The job with this id, only if it is a `job` job. Callers still check that the reader owns it. */
  get<J extends AnyJob>(job: J, id: string): Promise<JobInfo<DataOf<J>, ResultOf<J>> | null>;
  get(job: string, id: string): Promise<JobInfo | null>;
  enqueuer<J extends AnyJob>(job: J): Enqueuer<DataOf<J>>;
  definition(name: string): AnyJob;
  names(): string[];
  available(): Promise<boolean>;
  close(): Promise<void>;
}

/** Checks a set of definitions: unique names. Returns them by name. */
export function jobRegistry(jobs: readonly AnyJob[]): Map<string, AnyJob> {
  const byName = new Map<string, AnyJob>();
  for (const j of jobs) {
    if (byName.has(j.name)) throw new WorkerError("WORKER_DUPLICATE_JOB", `Two jobs are named "${j.name}"`);
    byName.set(j.name, j);
  }
  return byName;
}

export function createJobQueue(o: JobQueueOptions): JobQueue {
  const byName = jobRegistry(o.jobs);
  let closed = false;

  const resolve = (job: AnyJob | string): AnyJob => {
    const name = typeof job === "string" ? job : job.name;
    const def = byName.get(name);
    if (!def) throw new WorkerError("WORKER_UNKNOWN_JOB", `Unknown job "${name}" (known: ${[...byName.keys()].join(", ") || "none"})`);
    if (typeof job !== "string" && job !== def) throw new WorkerError("WORKER_UNKNOWN_JOB", `Job "${name}" is not the definition this queue was created with`);
    return def;
  };

  const enqueue = async (job: AnyJob | string, data: unknown, opts?: EnqueueOptions): Promise<JobInfo> => {
    if (closed) throw new WorkerError("WORKER_CLOSED", "The job queue is closed");
    const def = resolve(job);
    return o.backend.add(prepareJob(def, data, opts));
  };

  const available = async () => {
    if (closed) return false;
    try {
      return (await (o.backend.available?.() ?? true)) === true;
    } catch {
      return false;
    }
  };

  const queue: JobQueue = {
    mode: o.backend.mode,
    enqueue: enqueue as JobQueue["enqueue"],
    get: (async (job: AnyJob | string, id: string) => (typeof id === "string" && id ? o.backend.get(resolve(job), id) : null)) as JobQueue["get"],
    enqueuer(job) {
      const def = resolve(job);
      return {
        async enqueue(data) {
          const info = await enqueue(def, data);
          if (info.state === "failed") throw new WorkerError("WORKER_UNAVAILABLE", `Job "${def.name}" failed: ${info.error ?? "Job failed"}`);
          return info.id;
        },
        available,
      };
    },
    definition: (name) => resolve(name),
    names: () => [...byName.keys()],
    available,
    async close() {
      if (closed) return;
      closed = true;
      await o.backend.close();
    },
  };
  return queue;
}
```

## File: src/types.ts

```ts
// The job model shared by every backend. A job is JSON data on a named queue; a definition says
// how to run it. Backends (in-process, BullMQ on Redis, fallback) only move and store jobs.

/** A job's state, the same words on every backend. */
export type JobState = "waiting" | "delayed" | "active" | "completed" | "failed";

/** What a processor gets besides the data. */
export interface JobContext {
  id: string;
  name: string;
  queue: string;
  /** 1 on the first run, 2 on the first retry, … */
  attempt: number;
  /** Total attempts allowed. */
  attempts: number;
}

/**
 * A kind of background work. Data and result cross JSON (Dates arrive as ISO strings), on every
 * backend, so a job behaves the same in-process and on Redis.
 */
export interface JobDefinition<Data = unknown, Result = unknown> {
  /** Job name, unique in a queue set, e.g. "password-reset". */
  readonly name: string;
  /** Queue it runs on (Redis keys `<prefix>:<queue>:…`). Default: the name. */
  readonly queue: string;
  /** Runs before enqueueing, in the caller's request: throw (WorkerError WORKER_BAD_DATA) to refuse. */
  readonly validate?: ((data: Data) => void) | undefined;
  readonly process: (data: Data, ctx: JobContext) => Promise<Result> | Result;
  /** Total attempts, with exponential backoff between them. */
  readonly attempts: number;
  readonly backoffMs: number;
  /** How long a finished job (and its result) stays readable. 0 = removed at once. */
  readonly keepResultsMs: number;
  /** How long a failed job stays readable (at least a day by default, for inspection). */
  readonly keepFailedMs: number;
  /** Largest JSON payload accepted, in bytes. */
  readonly maxBytes: number;
  /** Refuse data with token / password / secret keys (see SECRET_KEY). */
  readonly refuseSecrets: boolean;
}

// eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any
export type AnyJob = JobDefinition<any, any>;
export type DataOf<J> = J extends JobDefinition<infer D, unknown> ? D : never;
export type ResultOf<J> = J extends JobDefinition<unknown, infer R> ? R : never;

/** A job as callers see it. */
export interface JobInfo<Data = unknown, Result = unknown> {
  id: string;
  name: string;
  queue: string;
  state: JobState;
  /** Attempts made so far. */
  attempts: number;
  /** Safe to show: a JobFailure's message, otherwise a generic "Job failed". */
  error: string | null;
  result: Result | null;
  data: Data;
  createdAt: Date;
  finishedAt: Date | null;
}

export interface EnqueueOptions {
  /** Run no sooner than this many ms from now. */
  delayMs?: number;
}

/** A job ready for a backend: JSON-checked data plus the backend-independent options. */
export interface PreparedJob {
  id: string;
  def: AnyJob;
  data: unknown;
  delayMs: number;
}

/**
 * Where jobs go. Implementations: `inlineBackend` (this process), `bullmqBackend` ("/bullmq",
 * Redis) and `fallbackBackend` (a worker when available, else standalone). Write your own the same way.
 */
export interface JobBackend {
  /** "inline", "bullmq", "fallback" or your own; shown in logs and health checks. */
  readonly mode: string;
  add(job: PreparedJob): Promise<JobInfo>;
  /** The job with this id on `def`'s queue, or null (unknown, expired, or another job's name). */
  get(def: AnyJob, id: string): Promise<JobInfo | null>;
  /** Cheap readiness check (e.g. the Redis connection is "ready"). Default: assume yes. */
  available?(): boolean | Promise<boolean>;
  close(): Promise<void>;
}
```
